Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short comparison and attached a PDF + a simple flow diagram for how a private-offer purchase flows end-to-end. High-level summary below (we can expand on any line).

Short answer: both paths are possible for BrightLeaf; recommended route depends on primary priorities.

Marketplace (Private Offer via AWS) — pros & cons- Invoice & billing: Customer appears on a consolidated AWS bill; AWS issues the invoice to the customer (seller-of-record depends on offer type). Private offer can route charges to BrightLeaf's AWS account and allow use of your existing procurement and PO process.
- Lead time: Private offer creation + acceptance typically 3–10 business days once pricing is agreed and AWS approves the offer.
- Discounts & co-sell credits: Eligible for co-sell credits if the transaction is registered per AWS partner program. Credits are applied to partner/rebates and reported via partner billing. BrightLeaf does not receive an additional Redwood invoice in most cases.
- Legal/tax: AWS standard terms cover transaction mechanics; however, you may still want a Redwood MSA for product-level terms. Tax treatment is handled on the AWS invoice in marketplace purchases (seller-of-record specifics vary by geography).
- Support/SLA: Support routing can be configured — marketplace purchases can still use Redwood support, but the support channel may go through marketplace support for initial triage depending on the offer.
- When to choose: fast procurement with existing AWS PO process, want consolidated AWS billing, minimal legal review of vendor terms.

Direct vendor (MSA + Redwood invoice/PO) — pros & cons- Invoice & billing: Redwood issues invoice directly to BrightLeaf; payment terms (Net30/Net45) are agreed with finance. Easier for non-AWS billing arrangements and for customers who require Redwood as seller-of-record.
- Lead time: Signing an MSA and SOW with redlines can take 2–4 weeks (variable based on legal review). For pilots we often use a short-form SOW to speed this up.
- Discounts & co-sell credits: Direct deals often provide more flexible discounts and custom payment terms but partner co-sell credits need to be handled via partner registration separately.
- Legal/tax: Full MSA gives explicit service commitments, indemnities, and data protections; tax treatment is on the Redwood invoice.
- Support/SLA: Direct routes typically provide the cleanest support routing (direct Redwood support queues, SLA tied to contract).
- When to choose: you need Redwood as seller-of-record, custom terms, or want support/SLA baked into the contract.

Recommendations for BrightLeaf pilot ($<25k/mo):
- If speed is top priority and you want to keep this under your AWS procurement flow: use an AWS Private Offer (marketplace) — it avoids a lengthy MSA review and fits existing PO processes.
- If you need explicit contract terms, data residency guarantees, or want Redwood to be seller-of-record: go direct with a short-form SOW + conditional MSA clause (we can offer a pilot addendum).

Thanks for the summary, Aditya — good framing. A few finance-specific notes for BrightLeaf's team: 

- Payment terms: For pilots we can offer Net30 by default; Net45 requires approval from Finance (possible for multi-month commitments).
- PO acceptance: If you use AWS Private Offer, the PO is accepted through AWS and we reconcile with AWS invoices. If you go direct, please send PO to billing@redwood.com and reference the SOW number.
- Tax forms: If BrightLeaf requires a reseller certificate or tax exemption, provide the certificate to billing@redwood.com; for marketplace purchases tax lines will appear on the AWS invoice and AWS handles collection by region.
- Invoices: Direct invoices include line items for seats/usage; marketplace invoices will be consolidated under AWS but we can provide sample invoice PDF for procurement.
- Discounts: For a pilot under $25k/mo we can offer a 10% pilot discount on list rates for direct purchases; marketplace private-offer discounts are supported but must be encoded in the private offer with AWS.

Attached is the Private_Offer_Checklist.xlsx we use internally — it lists the fields AWS requires to publish a private offer and the typical sign-off queue. 

Action required from BrightLeaf: please share the procurement contact full name, intended billing address for invoicing, and whether you prefer AWS consolidated billing or a Redwood invoice for your PO. That will determine the optimal path.

Happy to join a call with procurement to finalize.

Best,
Kimberly Park
